sentences.text: I broke my right hand, and typing notes got slow.
So I built Lucid, where my voice becomes structured notes, even with one hand.
I say a thought, or I type it.
Any dictation app that pastes text will do: Wispr Flow, OpenWhispr, or my own VoiceNative.
sentences.say: Any dictation app that pastes text will do: Whisper Flow, Open Whisper, or my own Voice Native.

sentences.text: A model on my own computer arranges it into a page: a heading, and a list.
Ask for a comparison, and it builds a table.
For a diagram, I say the parts, then how they connect.
Everything has a number, so a fix is one short sentence.
Then I say done, and the diagram is on my page.
Then Command mode. I say: add a cache in front of the database.
The diagram changes, and it is one undo step.
When it looks right, one click makes a clean PDF, typeset on my machine.
There are five note formats, from a single concept to a full system design.
They are plain data, so a lab notebook is just one more entry.
Lucid is also an MCP server, so an agent can read the page and add to it.
sentences.say: Lucid is also an M C P server, so an agent can read the page and add to it.

sentences.text: Every agent change shows up in the history.
Everything runs on your own computer, so it stays private.
Lucid is free and open source, on GitHub, under triggeredcode, slash lucid.
